title: When the Portrait Falls
premise: Emrys Halloran takes a teaching post at Hollowmere School, where a class vanished decades ago and the staff refuse to speak of it. When every mirror in their cottage begins reflecting one second behind reality, Emrys discovers the missing students were pulled into the reflection-world by a song the school still teaches — a lullaby whose final verse was never written down. To escape, Emrys must recover that verse from the last surviving singer, former headmistress Agnes Vane, without ever singing along, because each note sung inside the glass binds you deeper. In the end, Emrys learns the verse, refuses to sing it, and instead gives it away — shattering the mirrors, freeing the trapped class as ghosts who finally age and fade, at the cost of their own reflection, which remains behind in the glass forever.
about_author: Noor Underhill is the pen name of a former boarding-school matron who spent twenty years listening to what old buildings say after lights-out. They write horror about institutions, lullabies, and the people who stay too long.

chapters.title: The Position
chapters.summary: Emrys arrives at Hollowmere on a rain-gray evening, meeting headmaster Corvin Blake and the unnervingly quiet staff. A framed class photo from 1971 hangs with faces scratched out. POV: Emrys. Beat: uneasy hope — a fresh start that already feels like a trap.

chapters.title: First Bell
chapters.summary: Emrys teaches Year Nine and notices an empty desk no one acknowledges. A student, Wren Okafor, whispers that the desk belongs to 'the singing class.' POV: Emrys. Beat: curiosity sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Noises Have Explanations
chapters.summary: Nighttime sounds in the cottage — humming through the walls. Emrys catalogs rational causes aloud, a three-year habit of self-soothing. POV: Emrys. Beat: denial established as character armor.

chapters.title: Wren's List
chapters.summary: Wren shows Emrys a notebook listing eleven names of students gone missing across decades, all from the same classroom. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty forming between teacher and student against institutional silence.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: The bathroom mirror reflects Emrys raising a hand a beat after they do it. Then the hallway mirror. Then all of them. POV: Emrys. Beat: the rational armor cracks; terror becomes undeniable fact.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Emrys breaks into school records and finds the 1971 music syllabus: a lullaby called 'Hollowmere's Cradle,' its final page torn out. POV: Emrys. Beat: discovery — the song is the mechanism.

chapters.title: What Corvin Knows
chapters.summary: Confrontation with Headmaster Blake, who admits the disappearances but claims forgetting is mercy. He warns Emrys to leave before term ends. POV: Corvin. Beat: complicity revealed; the institution chose survival over truth.

chapters.title: Pulled Through
chapters.summary: At midnight the largest mirror liquefies and drags Emrys into the reflected cottage — identical, silent, wrong. Something hums the cradle song in another room. POV: Emrys. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Singing Class
chapters.summary: Inside the glass, Emrys finds the 1971 students, unaged, mouths moving in endless harmony. Their leader, Idris, begs Emrys not to hum along — even a bar binds you. POV: Idris. Beat: found family begins; the trapped become guides.

chapters.title: Rules of Glass
chapters.summary: Idris explains the world's laws: reflections repeat the past, time runs backward here, and the song's last verse is the door out — but only for those who know it without singing it. POV: Idris. Beat: stakes clarified; hope with a razor edge.

chapters.title: Wren on the Other Side
chapters.summary: Emrys watches through a mirror as Wren searches the cottage for them, calling their name into empty rooms. Emrys cannot be heard. POV: Wren. Beat: grief and guilt; love expressed as stubborn refusal to stop looking.

chapters.title: Backward Days
chapters.summary: Time reverses in the glass: Emrys's memories begin dissolving, oldest first. They carve their name into a windowsill daily to remember themselves. POV: Emrys. Beat: the price of survival made physical — losing who you are.

chapters.title: Agnes Vane
chapters.summary: Emrys escapes briefly through a mirror into the village and finds Agnes Vane, ninety-four, the last person taught the full song. She refuses to speak of it. POV: Emrys. Beat: the keeper of truth is also its prisoner.

chapters.title: The Verse That Was Cut
chapters.summary: Agnes reveals she tore out the page in 1971 to stop the song spreading, believing silence would starve it — instead it left the children stranded mid-verse. Her guilt has kept her alive and alone. POV: Agnes. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallized; her loyalty to the school cost eleven children.

chapters.title: Corvin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Blake catches Emrys outside the glass and offers a deal: his silence protected the school's funding for fifty years; he'll help if Emrys never exposes him. POV: Corvin. Beat: temptation — survival offered at the price of truth again.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Emrys rejects the bargain and returns through the glass carrying only the melody in memory, forbidden to sing it even once. The song inside them grows louder, hungry. POV: Emrys. Beat: resolve tested; the song wants to be finished.

chapters.title: Wren Follows
chapters.summary: Wren, refusing to wait, cuts their palm on a mirror and falls through. Now two lives hang on the unsung verse, and Wren starts humming without knowing why. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty endangers; Emrys must save someone else while drowning.

chapters.title: The Humming Deepens
chapters.summary: Wren slips toward the chorus; Emrys physically holds them back, nearly humming along themselves. Idris sacrifices his own fading memories to anchor them both. POV: Idris. Beat: sacrifice deepens the found family bond.

chapters.title: Last Verse, Unopened
chapters.summary: Emrys assembles the full song from Agnes's recitation and Idris's fragments — and realizes the final verse isn't sung at all. It must be given: spoken freely to someone who chooses to let go. POV: Emrys. Beat: revelation — the exit is surrender, not escape.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Glass
chapters.summary: At the great mirror, Emrys speaks the last verse aloud to the singing class, offering it without asking anything back. The song, unfinished by any single voice, loses its grip. POV: Emrys. Beat: climax — truth given freely defeats the bargain of survival.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Kept
chapters.summary: Every mirror shatters. The eleven students emerge as ghosts who finally age, thank Emrys, and fade into morning light. Wren wakes on the cottage floor. Emrys does not — their reflection stays behind, waving goodbye. POV: Wren. Beat: bittersweet release; the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Term Ends
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wren visits Emrys, who now casts no reflection anywhere yet lives, warm and real, teaching again. Together they visit Agnes, who finally weeps. The scratched photo shows eleven smiling faces. POV: Wren. Beat: resolution — found family endures beyond glass, and truth outlives the price.
